places.name: Statue of Liberty
places.desc: Statue of Liberty takes about 4 to 5 hours to complete the full tour, including travel and security.

places.name: New York Crown
places.desc: Access to the interior (pedestal or crown) requires specialized tickets that often sell out 4 to 6 months in advance.

places.name: Ellis Island National Museum of Immigration
places.desc: General admission includes the museum and the documentary film. If you want a unique experience, look into booking the 90-minute Hard Hat Tour of the abandoned immigrant hospital complex. You can also search for family arrival records at the American Family Immigration History Center.

places.name: Empire State Building
places.desc: There are multiple ticket tiers. The standard ticket gets you to the 86th-floor open-air observatory. It is highly recommended to buy tickets in advance to skip the standard ticket purchasing line. Plan for about 1.5 to 2 hours for the visit.

places.name: Times Square
places.desc: Visiting after dark is a must to really experience the famous glowing billboards and neon lights. It is an incredible environment to bring your Sony α6600 out for some dynamic, high-contrast night photography. Expect heavy crowds, costumed street performers, and a very fast-paced atmosphere.

places.name: Brooklyn Bridge
places.desc: Walking the 1.1-mile span takes about 30 to 60 minutes, depending on your pace and the crowds. Early morning just after sunrise or late evening provides excellent lighting and more space for capturing the stone arches and the Manhattan skyline with the Sony α6600. Just be sure to stay in the designated pedestrian lane to avoid the fast-moving commuter cyclists!

places.name: Grand Central Terminal
places.desc: There is a lot to see inside. Make sure to look up at the famous celestial ceiling mural in the Main Concourse and check out the four-faced opal clock on top of the information booth. Downstairs, you can test out the acoustic trick of the "Whispering Gallery" outside the Oyster Bar. For photography, setting up on the balconies to capture the light streaming through the massive arched windows or using a slightly slower shutter speed to capture the motion blur of the rushing commuters makes for a great shot.

places.name: Central Park
places.desc: Because the park covers 843 acres, it is best to pick a specific section to explore rather than trying to walk the entire length. The southern half is the most famous and includes iconic spots like Bethesda Terrace, Bow Bridge, and the Mall. If you have your camera with you, the contrast between the natural foliage and the towering skyscrapers surrounding the park makes for excellent framing.

places.name: The High Line
places.desc: Built on an abandoned elevated freight rail line, this park sits 30 feet above the street. The elevated vantage point gives you unique, unobstructed angles of the avenues and yellow cabs directly below, making it an excellent location to shoot with your Sony α6600. It also runs right past Chelsea Market, which is a perfect place for you and Beatrix to step off the path and grab some fantastic food.

places.name: Little Island
places.address: Pier 55 at Hudson River Park, New York, NY 10014
places.desc: This is a striking, highly unique public park built entirely on tulip-shaped concrete stilts suspended right over the Hudson River. It features lush flower beds, rolling hills, and fantastic overlooks. Because it is located just a few blocks away from the southern end of the High Line, it makes perfect sense to do both on the same afternoon. The strange, futuristic architecture and waterside sunset views make it another great spot to bring out the Sony α6600.
